daily_report_items: PLS.AX first full review completed: AUD1.67/AUD3.67/AUD6.69 scenarios imply AUD3.925 weighted value versus AUD5.40; deterministic rating is Sell / Avoid and allocation remains ineligible. The 32.35% alert-period rally and volume anomaly do not justify a strategy. One dependent lithium-cycle relationship review was queued.

evidence.claim: PLS reported FY2026 revenue of AUD2.017 billion, underlying EBITDA of AUD1.137 billion, AUD809 million NPAT, 879.5 thousand tonnes of production, AUD2.290 billion cash and a 5-cent final dividend; the audited report also supports the debt, lease and project-risk inputs.

PLS guided FY2027 spodumene production to 1.03-1.10 million tonnes and FOB operating cost to AUD575-625 per tonne while reporting 1.2 million tonnes per annum installed capacity, a 31-year Pilgangoora mine life and P2000 and Colina growth work.

The canonical 3 August through 31 August 2026 observation records a 32.35% rise to AUD5.400000095367432 and a volume anomaly with strength 0.168819695; deterministic measurements were treated as data and not recalculated.

Deterministic schema-version-two output records AUD3.925 weighted fair value, -27.31481609848135798806922015% expected return, medium-confidence adjusted expected return of -20.48611207386101849105191511%, Sell / Avoid and ineligibility for base-return, payoff, expected-return, margin-of-safety and relationship gates.

summary: Completed the first full research review of PLS Group Limited ordinary shares. Current FY2026 issuer evidence supports a scaled, low-cost and long-life Pilgangoora operation with a strong net-cash balance sheet, but the canonical AUD1.67/AUD3.67/AUD6.69 scenarios produce AUD3.925 probability-weighted value against the AUD5.400000095367432 mark. Deterministic assessment output is Sell / Avoid, allocation-ineligible, with no strategy or paper order. The 32.35% alert-period rise and volume anomaly are explained partly by current results and guidance but do not create an attractive entry. One dependent relationship review was queued for the lithium-cycle candidate; no candidate was represented as accepted.
